# git: command: pull must respect tagopt

Stop `pull` from importing tags from template repositories. **Motivation:** the author registers GitHub template repositories as `upstream` to fetch their later improvements ([[DOT-172]]), but templates carry their own tags; `pull` fetches `--tags` from every remote and the next `push` sends those tags to `origin`. Git's per-remote `remote.<name>.tagopt --no-tags` ([explained here](https://www.feliciano.tech/blog/tell-git-dont-fetch-tags/)) is the switch; `pull` should honour it — or set it for `upstream`. Example pair: [obsidianmd/obsidian-sample-plugin](https://github.com/obsidianmd/obsidian-sample-plugin) as the template of [withsparkle/obsidian](https://github.com/withsparkle/obsidian).

<!-- 2026-09-16T05:49Z https://github.com/kamilsk/dotfiles/issues/637#issuecomment-5711709571
Code vs intent: `git-pull` passes an explicit `--tags`, which overrides `remote.<name>.tagopt --no-tags`; setting `tagopt` on `upstream` alone will not stop the tag import. The flag has to be dropped (rely on auto-following + `tagopt`) or tags fetched only from the tracked remote. `git-push --tags` to all non-fork remotes then propagates whatever was imported.
